label: input token v at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires only when the input is the letter v during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at positions 2 through 6. It never fires on v at positions 0, 1, 7 or 8, never on the delimiter, and never in the copy phase (including when v is fed back as an output). Every active step is an input v. Magnitude depends on position: weak at t=2 (about 0.1-0.3 of max), strongest at t=3-5 (top examples are v at t=4, about 1.0 of max), and lower again at t=6, where a few v inputs (around 98 on dev) do not fire at all. Repeated v (not the first occurrence) gets a smaller share of activation. Other tokens have no visible effect on magnitude.

issues: Minor overclaim: 'a repeated v carries less activation mass' is true only in total. Per step it is not lower. Repeated v (in_first==0) makes up 11.5% of active test steps and 11.6% of activation mass, so the per-step magnitude matches first occurrences.

The false positives are all at t=6 (92 on test, out of 8208 v inputs at t=6, about 1.1%). Splitting by L shows no pattern: precision is 0.988 for L=7 and 0.989 for L>7. This looks like scattered noise near the edge of the position window, not a systematic class.

Every other claim checks out on dev: no activity in the delimiter or copy phase, none at t=0,1 or t>=7, and only input v ever fires. The magnitude profile also matches: t=2 has 0.081 of the mass from 16.7k steps, while t=3-5 carry most of it. The test split shows 0 missed activations. Restricting the predicate to t 2-5 gives precision 1.0, but recall drops to 0.877, so including t=6 is correct.
